The Phase 1/2 driver (`ledger-driver.py`, ruling A8b) consumes the JSON: every executable row's `path` is a JSON array of globs (old-tree globs relative to this repository root; flows-tree globs prefixed `flows:` and relative to the flows root; brace alternatives and `**` allowed, no brace ranges, prose, counts or absolute paths), and every executable row matches at least one file in `git ls-tree -r --name-only <revision>` of its tree (old `9169a943eb`, flows `393253c2b`). The most specific matching row owns a file; 71 rows carry `executable: false` (findings, gaps, decisions, limits, human tasks, Plue items, command groups implemented inside one file, root-wiring notes and the flows "not imported" note) and keep a descriptive `path` string plus a unique `key`, which the driver skips. `label` is the human-readable name shown in the Label column below; `section` is the table the row belongs to; `maintainerDecisions` holds the 18 decision rows and `orchestratorRulings` the cycle-1 rulings. The Path column of every table shows the row's globs joined by spaces, or `(advisory)`. Checks: `python3 <scratch>/ledger-driver.py check --ledger docs/migration/disposition-ledger.json --v1 . --flows-repo /Users/williamcory/flows/flows` printed zero PROBLEM lines, zero uncovered and zero ambiguous v1 files and zero ambiguous flows files on 2026-08-28 (9,504 tracked old files covered, 2,986 of 3,602 flows files imported, the 616 others listed in the "flows files not imported" note row); `node docs/migration/check-disposition-ledger.mjs` validates the schema, every glob and this Markdown twin; `docs/migration/phase1-2-plan.json` is the per-file plan the driver wrote from this ledger and commits before deletion.

## What this ledger is

PLAN.md Phase 0 requires a disposition for every tracked top-level area of the old repository before anything is deleted, and Phase 2 requires a copy plan for the imported tree. This document records both. Every row cites the reader findings file it came from (`[area §n]`) or a command the writer ran on 2026-08-28. Where readers disagreed or left an open question, the row's rationale opens with `Ruling` and states the decision and its evidence; where a review-cycle ruling changed a row, the rationale opens with `Orchestrator ruling` and names it.

## Vocabulary

| Disposition | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `replace`   | Superseded by an imported flows package or file. The old path is removed in Phase 1; the successor lands in Phase 2 (or is assembled in Phase 4 where the successor is not yet a server).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `migrate`   | Behavior is retained but rewritten against the new public APIs. Where the old code cannot compile after Phase 1 (marked `[phase1-removal]` in Notes) it is removed in Phase 1 and ported from `cfb570f193`; the driver moves other migrate files to `legacy/<path>` in Phase 1, except files inside a `keep` subtree (rewritten in place in Phase 4) and root files (reconciled in place; Phase 2 writes a `.flows` twin).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `keep`      | Independent of the runtime and retained in place. Ruling on the vocabulary: PLAN.md:107 says "safe to retain unchanged"; this ledger applies it as "retained in place" and allows hygiene edits that are named in the new-home column (ignore entries, a prepended changelog section, a "written for 0.x" banner, a build-config conversion, a re-checked hint string). Any edit that rewrites content or code against the new APIs or the new invocation is `migrate`, not `keep` (the `docs/index.mdx` and `docs/reference/sota-models.mdx` rows were moved for that reason). PLAN.md:141-143 requires the plan to follow a changed reading, so the Phase 0 commit that lands this ledger widens PLAN.md:107 to the same wording. A `delete` or `replace` row inside a keep subtree carries `allowInsideKeep: true` with the reason in Notes (A8c). |
| `delete`    | Obsolete, duplicated, generated, or a superseded proof of concept. Recoverable from `cfb570f193` (old tree) or the import reference tag (flows tree). On the flows-side note row it means excluded from the Phase 2 copy. On a Phase 5 row keyed by a finding id it means an exclusion whose enforcement is named in the new-home column.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `import`    | Copied from the flows tree in Phase 2 (`git archive 393253c2b -- <path>`). The sixth PLAN.md Phase 0 disposition (ruling A8; PLAN.md Phase 0 names it): a flows-side area copied in Phase 2, on rows whose `tree` is `flows`; root files that need reconciliation with a surviving old file are marked `[reconcile]` in the old row's Notes. Phase 5 rows are keyed by finding id and carry `tree: flows` because they act on imported code; they are advisory.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

Phase numbers follow PLAN.md: 1 delete, 2 import/reconcile, 3 versioning and release contract, 4 migrate retained functionality, 5 correctness and parity gaps, 6 migration workflow, 7 RC validation, `-` no phase (kept as-is, or work scheduled after `1.0.0-rc.0` as the new-home column states). `decide` entries: 0.

## Rulings on reader open questions

Every open question raised by a reader is resolved below by the most conservative disposition consistent with PLAN.md (delete for POCs and demos, migrate for product requirements with consumer evidence, keep only for runtime-independent items). The row that carries each ruling repeats it.

Old execution core: (1) `packages/control-plane` is deleted outright, not moved. (2) No read-only importer for completed 0.x history in rc.0; `smithers.db` is archive-only and Phase 5 adds a startup guard against old `_smithers_*` tables. (3) `@smthrs/errors` is `migrate`, not delete (orchestrator ruling A1, decided by grep evidence): `packages/integrations`, which ruling A7 makes `migrate`, imports it from 11 source files that migrate (core/{IntegrationError.js,signalNames.js,CursorStoreTypes.ts}, github/GitHubClientService.ts, linear/{LinearClient.js,LinearClientTypes.ts}, telegram/{TelegramClient.js,TelegramClientTypes.ts,approval.js,config.js,initData.js}; the row's evidence lists every importer per row), so the package is trimmed to the error types those consumers use and stays a private workspace package; the three apps/cli modules rewritten into packages/cli switch to `CliError` and every plugins-repository module drops the dependency there; `rc-contract.md` R-34 records the same ruling.

Gateway and UI: (1) The RC gateway is assembled in Phase 4 in `packages/gateway` from `ControlServer` + `SyncServer`/`BranchServer` handlers + a durable `RunCatalog`, hosted by `smithers serve`, and serves the Plue floor through the RC bindings in `rc-contract.md` §10: `List flows`; `Plan` + `Approve` (scope `run`) + `Run` for a launch; `List runs` (with a `runId` filter) for a run summary; the `approvals`, `node-output` and `transcript` projections plus the `run-summary` diagnosis; `Cancel`; and `Watch` over `/rpc/ws` with heartbeat frames. The 0.x names (listWorkflows, launchRun, getRun, listApprovals, submitApproval, getNodeOutput, whatHappened, cancelRun, streamRunEvents) describe the capabilities Plue needs, not served methods: no 0.x method name or path is served (`rc-contract.md` §7 Gateway, R-8; plue-consumer-contract P2). (2) rc.0 ships one run UI, `apps/ui`; `smithers monitor`, `smithers ui`, `smithers gui`, `smithers-mon` and the packages gateway-react, gateway-ui, ui-core, tui, tui-ui, devtools are deleted and gateway-client is replaced by `@smthrs/control` ControlClient + `@smthrs/sync` SyncClient; `ui` and `ui-styleguide` are kept. (3) Plue's relay forwards one bearer token to `POST /rpc` and `WS /rpc/ws` (single principal, `ControlRpcs.layerBearerAuth`); the `/v1/rpc/*` path shape and the 14-scope model are not carried. (4) Run and node diff views and jumpToFrame are dropped; the pure `@smthrs/ui` diff primitives stay. (5) whatHappened is rebuilt from the journal through the CLI Forensics digest. (6) Flows `apps/ui/.smithers` is excluded from the Phase 2 copy and used as a Phase 6 fixture from the tag.

Agents and capabilities: (1) The Pi inspector is deleted with a release note; no successor in rc.0. (2) Claude Code and Codex (maintainer lanes and Plue Path A), Kimi (maintainer seat policy: Kimi K3 is a deliberate seat) and Antigravity (a non-pack Plue consumer, `plue/e2e/api/smithers-agent-system.test.ts:371-380`; Gemini as a rewrite rule) migrate to the plugins repository; Cursor, Amp (its only Plue references are in the Phase 6 fixture pack `.smithers/agents.ts:9,48`), Grok, OMP, OpenClaw, Vibe, Forge, Hermes CLI, Pool, Pi and OpenCode are deleted and listed as unsupported. (3) The account registry and `fallbackAgents` seat pool move to the plugins repository as a `SeatResolver` implementation; core keeps only the seam; the quota park/wake driver is excluded. (4) The canonical plugins repository is `github.com/smithersai/plugins` (`smithers-plugins` redirects to it); it must be renamed to `@smthrs/*` and rebased on the current kernel/platform seams before Phase 4 ports land; nothing lands in core meanwhile. Its `main` branch (5334a01, pushed 2026-08-06) holds the packages `adapters` (named `@smithers/adapters` there), `agent`, `flows`, `host-cloudflare` and `host-vercel`; the local clone `/Users/williamcory/flows/plugins` is two unpushed commits ahead on `preflight/oneshot-msspasmr-2133c832` (afdfda7, 2026-08-14) and already names the package `@smthrs/adapters`, so the rename is pushed from that branch before any port lands; the older clone `/Users/williamcory/smithers-plugins` (origin `smithersai/smithers-plugins`, bfda99a, 2026-07-29, `@flows/adapters`) is superseded and is not evidence. `host-cloudflare` and `host-vercel` there import the `@smthrs/host` package that flows deleted in `94bab62b9`, so they are port targets, not existing replacements (rows `packages/cloudflare`, `packages/vercel`). (5) `smithers memory` and `steer` ship in rc.0; `agents` (including its `capabilities` and `doctor` subcommands), `openapi`, `eval`, `scores`, `top`, `herdr`, `hijack` are hidden unsupported verbs (`rc-contract.md` §4.2); `smithers doctor` is the flows system verb, not the old `agents doctor`.

Hosts and integrations: (1) The five `@smthrs/jj-<platform>` packages, `scripts/fetch-jj-binaries.mjs` and the root pins are deleted; jj is a documented system requirement; `SMITHERS_JJ_PATH` and the doctor probe migrate into the `NodeJj` resolver. (2) No vendor sandbox provider is an rc.0 gate: Cloudflare and Vercel migrate to the plugins packages `host-cloudflare` and `host-vercel`, which must first be re-ported from the deleted `@smthrs/host` onto the `@smthrs/kernel` and `@smthrs/platform-*` seams (33 `@smthrs/host` imports today), Microsandbox migrates to a new plugins package, AWS/GCP/Daytona are deleted. (3) Orchestrator ruling A7 (reversible): the GitHub, Linear and Telegram client, authentication, webhook-verification (constant-time HMAC), cursor, rate-limit and error-classification code in `packages/integrations/src/{core,github,linear,telegram}` and `packages/accounts/src/{pkce,buildAuthorizationUrl}.js`, with their behavior tests, `migrate` to a rebuilt `@smthrs/integrations` (private at rc.0) on the new action, notification and trigger APIs in Phase 4; the JSX components, the old-engine delivery runtime and `packages/telegram` are deleted or replaced; GitHub and Linear are rc.0's real integrations and satisfy the Phase 7 "exercise one real integration" smoke. (4) Plugins-repository readiness is a Phase 4 prerequisite the maintainer owns (rulings A7/E2; `rc-contract.md` §10): `/Users/williamcory/smithers-plugins` imports `@flows/*` and `/Users/williamcory/flows/plugins` imports the deleted `@smthrs/host`; neither has a seat-resolver, accounts, usage or microsandbox package; exit condition: the plugins repository rebased onto `@smthrs/*` 1.0.0-rc.0 with those packages present. Every row whose new home is the plugins repository carries the prerequisite in Notes. (5) Sandboxed child flow with a diff-review gate is an exclusion (G-10). (6) Broadcast signal delivery is not in rc.0. (7) `@smthrs/electric-proxy` deletion confirmed. (8) Both Telegram clients go. (9) The `system/doctor` body is implemented in `packages/cli` in Phase 4.

CLI: (1) Accounts pool: plugins repository. (2) `serve` is the real verb; bare `gateway` is an alias of `serve` for rc.0 and is removed at 1.0.0 (`rc-contract.md` R-14); `gateway status|stop` are hidden unsupported verbs. (3) The 21 semantic MCP tool names are kept: 11 Control-backed (`list_workflows`, `run_workflow`, `list_runs`, `get_run`, `watch_run`, `get_run_events`, `explain_run`, `list_pending_approvals`, `resolve_approval`, `get_node_detail`, `get_chat_transcript`), 10 return an unsupported result, `ask_human` among them because it is built on the deleted `@smthrs/engine/human-requests` module and the deleted `human answer` verb and flows `Control` has no question or answer RPC (`rc-contract.md` §4.1, R-15; triage W-20). (4) `review` is not an rc.0 verb (`rc-contract.md` R-16): it is a hidden unsupported verb, and `apps/review` migrates with its own `smithers-review` bin. (5) Flows `apps/ui/.smithers` is excluded from the copy. (6) Detached launch (`up -d`) stays; the liveness answer is Phase 5 item GAP-2.

Other apps: (1) `apps/review` migrates; `pr-review.yml` and the README pin the action to `cfb570f193` in the Phase 1 commit. (2) No local browser UI command. (3) Worker teardown is a maintainer ops action outside the repository; worker names are recorded in the rows. (4) `apps/quota-dashboard` is deleted. (5) `smithers bug` stays, so `apps/bug-worker` stays. (6) research-site and kimi-benchmarks-site are deleted outright. (7) The agent-trace normalization group is deleted; redaction requirements target `@smthrs/journal`. (8) Prometheus `/metrics` is excluded; export is OTLP only.

Examples: (1) custom-sandbox.smithers.sh stays as last deployed until torn down; source deleted. (2) Flows examples 01-15 are at the import reference and are imported (12-15, `a47cddcda`, are live smoke runs that need a credential or a local server); new examples start at 16. (3) swe-evo results are not archived. (4) Example 23 (triggers) is not authored; 25 (sandbox seam) and 26 (memory) stay because those packages are public.

Docs: (1) Orchestrator ruling A2 (reversible): vocs wins. PLAN Phase 0 says the imported repository's tooling baseline wins unless a current Smithers release requirement proves otherwise, and Mintlify hosting is a deployment, not a repository requirement. `vocs.config.ts`, `patches/vocs@2.8.5.patch`, `docs/pages/**` and `docs/pages.gen.ts` are `import`; `docs/docs.json`, the Mintlify-only assets and the `llms*.txt` bundles are `replace` (regenerated by the vocs pipeline in Phase 4); old Mintlify pages that survive are rewritten as vocs pages under `docs/pages`; the Phase 4 docs lane re-provides `pnpm docs:llms`, `check-docs` and `check-llms` on the vocs tree and adds the docs deploy workflow for smithers.sh (flows has none today). `rc-contract.md` R-25 records this ruling; it supersedes the earlier docs Q1 ruling (Mintlify stays). (2) Documented invocation: `npm install -g @smthrs/cli` (exposes `smithers`) and one-shot `npx --package @smthrs/cli smithers`; `bunx smthrs` is retired. (3) The three custom landing pages are rewritten as vocs pages. (4) Dated why/ articles get a "written for 0.x" banner. (5) The 44 changelog pages stay (no changelog uses a Mintlify component; verified 2026-08-28). (6) The `docs` command and the curated skill bundle survive; mirrors are regenerated. Plue's dead `docs.smithers.sh/llms-full.txt` URL is repointed to `smithers.sh/llms-full.txt` in its cutover.

Workflow pack and skills: (1) `--mcp` ships. (2) The Claude `/workflows` mirror and background monitor are retained over `Control.watch` (contract v2). (3) The account pool is excluded from core (plugins repository); the skill is deleted. (4) Only `init` is re-provided; `add`, `remove`, `eject` and `packs` are hidden unsupported verbs (`rc-contract.md` R-7); post-failure, upgrade, create-workflow, create-skill, create-ui, eval-suite-run, share-pack are release-note exclusions (the create-* prompt bodies seed Phase 6). (5) Per-command skill generation is dropped; `skills add` installs the curated skill. (6) release-content automation is dropped; the root `release:*`/`marketing:*` scripts go. (7) `lib/plue-provider.ts` is deleted (exclusion G-10; no Plue production consumer).

Tooling, tests, CI: (1) Bundled jj: delete. (2) `1.0.0-rc.N` publishes under the `next` dist-tag (flows default). (3) No GitHub release automation. (4) Windows stays advisory. (5) The nightly soak and 100-pass promotion mechanism are dropped; one PR-time e2e job plus the in-process FaultMatrix harness. (6) llms bundles stay a 1.0 deliverable, regenerated from the vocs tree (A2). (7) Agent-fluency evals are deleted. (8) `pr-review.yml` is pinned, not disabled.

Flows packages: (1) The private build CLI renames its bin from `smthrs` to `smithers-build` in Phase 3 (`rc-contract.md` R-1, §3.4): PLAN requires the `smthrs` bin to be resolved before packing and `check-local-smithers` scans for the deprecated package name in execution position. (2) `@smthrs/testing` and `@smthrs/gateway` are public (`rc-contract.md` §3 rules (b) and (c): `smithers serve` composes the projection server in `packages/gateway`, which puts it in `@smthrs/cli`'s dependency closure); `chain` is private at rc.0. (3) `@smthrs/build` is private. (4) `@smthrs/mcp` is in rc.0 and public (`rc-contract.md` R-4, §3 rule (a)): `packages/mcp` (`074b5bd3d`) and the CLI `--mcp-config` wiring (`31b0a5e6e`) are at the import reference `393253c2b`, and `packages/cli/package.json:95` depends on the package. (5) Dist-tag `next`.

Flows CLI and control: (0) Orchestrator ruling A6: the `replay` CLI verb is unsupported at rc.0 (exit 1, migration message; hidden subcommand, `rc-contract.md` R-7 and §4.2, triage W-17 and the negative command gate X-19); library time travel (replay, fork, rewind) stays. (1) Project flows live in `flows/<name>/flow.{ts,mdx}` and runtime state in `.flows/`; the flows `/flows` ignore rule is not taken so tracked workflow code (Phase 6 `flows/migrate-smithers-v1`) lives under `flows/`; `.smithers/` stays the ignored 0.x pack name. (2) Reserved system verbs `serve`, `up`, `init`, `doctor` and `docs` get bodies in Phase 4 and `migrate` in Phase 6; `release`, `replay`, `add`, `remove`, `eject` and `test` fail with `CliError.UnsupportedError` (`rc-contract.md` R-7). (3) The RC gateway serves the control/sync RPCs plus the Plue floor projections; the full `GatewaySchema.ProjectionName` set is not required before rc.0.

Flows apps, docs, release: (1) The eight Workers in `~/flows/ui/workers/` remain an external deployment outside rc.0 scope. (2) vocs (above, ruling A2). (3) LICENSE wording kept as owner-confirmed. (4) Tracked workflow code lives under `flows/` (above). (5) The canary.smithers.sh deployment and its hourly `canary.yml` job are deferred and are not an rc.0 validation surface; the `apps/server` code retarget is part of the Plue cutover, which itself stays a Phase 7 publish gate (`rc-contract.md` §10, R-27).

Phase 5 gaps: (1) The `Pause` RPC and every `pause` member (`Control`, `ControlLive`, `layerNoop`, `ControlRuntime`, `SqlControlRuntime`) are removed (`rc-contract.md` R-9, triage X-03 and W-04); the consumer inventory (Plue, `apps/ui`, the retained UI packages) confirms no caller, and the fence tests move to `writeStatus(runId, fence, 'parked')`, the same transition `pause` performed. (2) G-02 is verified (triage R-2): Effect's Node spawner already places each child in its own process group and kills the group on scope release; the fix is a `forceKillAfter` default in `packages/std` `Exec.ts` and `packages/kernel` `ChildProcessSpawner.ts` (W-14), not a wrapper in `packages/platform-node`. (3) One documented retention command suffices for rc.0. (4) Old case22 is a Phase 7 parity target; case28 folds into the F-17 bounded fan-out test. (5) Node approval does not resume the run server-side at the import reference: `ControlLive.decide` installs the grant and resolves the token but journals only `control.approval.<decision>`, and the executor's resume bridge reacts only to `control.run.resume`/`control.run.resumed`; this is blocker B-15 (triage R-11, W-19) rather than the "Present" the consumer-contract reader recorded. (6) Durable retry bounds are verified, not a defect (triage R-9): action `RetryPolicy` attempt counts and the `expirationMs` origin are persisted by the durable driver; only the suspended-flow polling budget is per invocation by design (F-11 stays a docs item). (7) The `unsupported_runtime` guard for Bun that `rc-contract.md` §1 and §7 promise is scheduled in W-16 beside the database-file guard (rows X-13 and X-18).

Plue: Plue source rows are not in this ledger (Plue is read-only in Phase 0 and is migrated with Smithers under D18). The two Plue decisions raised by the consumer-contract reader are recorded in the `Plue cutover decisions` section: D1 (the TSX CI DSL) is Plue's own decision in shape, split into a `keep` row for the engine-free static renderer and a `migrate` row for the `@smithers-ai/workflow` package, which imports `createSmithers` and the JSX components from `smithers-orchestrator` today and is rewritten under the rc.0 gate (`rc-contract.md` R-19, §10); D2 (tier-2 dev-automation survivors) resolves to an empty re-author list, every tier-2 workflow being a Phase 6 fixture (R-21; `pair-poc.tsx` was deleted from Plue at `2db1ecff2` and is no longer on the list). The Plue survey revision `8e03dbe5d2` is the authority for every Plue count; the delta to `2db1ecff2` is recorded in `plue-consumer-contract.md` §1; Plue HEAD on 2026-08-28 is `664c95c60` (three commits after `2db1ecff2`, tracing and observe features, no smithers-import file touched) and the live working tree is dirty and is never an authority (ruling E9). The consumer contract findings fix the rc.0 floor cited above.

## Deletion set for Phase 1

The Phase 1 change removes three sets in one bounded commit (version control is the recovery mechanism; every path is recoverable from `cfb570f193`). It also pins `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml` and the apps/review README to `apps/review/action@cfb570f193`, removes the `.smithers` and `codex-plugin` entries from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, drops the root `release:*`/`marketing:*`/`generate:init-pack`/`sota:*`/`typecheck:*` scripts, and refreshes both lockfiles.

The driver executes this set from `phase1-2-plan.json`: delete and replace rows are `git rm`; migrate rows outside a keep subtree move to `legacy/<path>` (in place when marked `[phase1-removal]` they are removed and ported from `cfb570f193` later); the `trellis` gitlink and its `.gitmodules` entry go with the trellis row.

Ruling (gateway-and-ui Q8, cli Q5): excluded from the Phase 2 copy; the flows/apps reader records the exclusion here. \| apps/ui/{FLOW-REUSE-RECEIPT.md,MANUAL-REVIEW-CHECKLIST.md}: Receipts of the 2026-08-19 web-app era whose build path was removed 2026-08-26. \| apps/MIGRATION.md + apps/WAVE*-RECEIPT.md (15 files): History of smithersai/mvp -> apps/mvp -> split; archaeology only, available at the import tag. \| apps/reports/** (84 files, 4.9M): CI artifact output directory, not source. \| docs/release-rehearsal.md: A dated receipt, not a living document. \| factory/reports/**: One-off outputs written by factory/flows/coverage-baseline.ts. \| .smithers/** (root, 23 files): Pure old-engine JSX workflows force-added past the flows .gitignore; PLAN Phase 1 material. \| {HUMAN-TASKS.md,MIGRATION-NOTES.md,PACKAGE-API-CHECKLIST.md,PLAN.md,REVIEW.md,.file-routing-codex-draft.md,.file-routing-fable-draft.md}: Ruling on the reader disagreement over PACKAGE-API-CHECKLIST.md (flows-gaps: keep; flows-apps: do not import): not imported, because it is developer planning state with machine-local paths (/Users/williamcory/artsy*), unrelated to the engine, and rewritten in the import-reference commit 393253c2b itself; flows PLAN.md is an unrelated routing plan that would clobber the migration plan; REVIEW.md and HUMAN-TASKS.md are superseded alpha artifacts (all still-open items are carried by the Phase 5 rows). \| Uncommitted flows working-tree edits after 393253c2b: the import is git archive 393253c2b, so edits upstream had not committed when the reference was pinned are not imported; at 2026-08-28 22:49 PDT (51 under apps/ui, 13 under apps/shared, 4 under apps/server, pnpm-lock.yaml, .file-routing-fable-draft.md) the flows working tree carried 70 uncommitted tracked modifications, all under import rows at their 393253c2b content.
